# Neo4j Query Receiver

The Neo4j Query Receiver uses custom Cypher queries to generate logs and/or metrics from a Neo4j database connection.

> :construction: This receiver is in **DEVELOPMENT**. Behavior, configuration fields, and the metric data model are
> subject to change. It is a fork-only component of the `attributecache-collector` distribution and is not part of
> upstream opentelemetry-collector-contrib.

The receiver is the Neo4j counterpart of the [SQL Query Receiver](../sqlqueryreceiver/README.md): every collection
interval it runs the configured Cypher statements over the Bolt protocol and turns each returned row into a metric
data point or a log record. The `metrics` and `logs` sections of a query use the same keys as the SQL Query Receiver,
so existing `sql_query` definitions can be reused with minimal changes.

## Configuration

**Connection:**

- `uri` (required): Bolt URI of the server or cluster, e.g. `bolt://localhost:7687`, `neo4j://cluster:7687`,
  `neo4j+s://xxxx.databases.neo4j.io`. The scheme selects routing and TLS behavior exactly as documented by the
  [Neo4j Go driver](https://neo4j.com/docs/go-manual/current/connect-advanced/#_connection_uri): `neo4j` enables
  cluster routing, `bolt` connects to a single server; `+s` enables TLS with certificate verification, `+ssc` enables
  TLS with self-signed certificates.
- `username` (optional): account used for basic authentication. Leave both `username` and `password` empty for
  servers that allow unauthenticated access.
- `password` (optional): password for basic authentication. Supports environment variable substitution
  (`${env:NEO4J_PASSWORD}`) and is redacted in logs and debug output.
- `database` (optional): the database to run the queries against. Defaults to the server's default database.
- `max_connection_pool_size` (optional, default `0`): maximum number of pooled Bolt connections. `0` keeps the
  driver default of 100.

**Collection:**

- `queries` (required): list of queries, see below.
- `collection_interval` (optional, default `10s`): time between query executions.
- `initial_delay` (optional, default `1s`): how long the receiver waits before the first collection.
- `timeout` (optional, default `0s`): maximum duration of a single query execution before it is cancelled. A
  non-positive value disables the timeout.
- `storage` (optional, default `""`): the ID of a [storage extension][storage_extension] used to persist the
  tracking value of logs queries across collector restarts, see [Tracking processed results](#tracking-processed-results).
- `telemetry.logs.query` (optional, default `false`): when `true`, the Cypher text and parameters of every executed
  query are logged at debug level together with the message `Running query`.

[storage_extension]: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/tree/main/extension/storage/filestorage

The driver connects lazily, so the collector starts even when the database is unreachable. Connection and query
errors are logged, reported through the component status API as recoverable errors, and retried on the next
collection interval.

### Queries

A _query_ consists of a Cypher statement and one or more `logs` and/or `metrics` definitions. At least one `logs`
or one `metrics` section is required. A metrics pipeline only runs queries with a `metrics` section and a logs
pipeline only runs queries with a `logs` section.

- `cypher` (required): the statement to execute. It must `RETURN` named columns; the names (aliases) are matched
  against `value_column`, `attribute_columns`, `ts_column`, `start_ts_column` and `row_condition.column`.
- `parameters` (optional): map of [Cypher query parameters](https://neo4j.com/docs/cypher-manual/current/syntax/parameters/)
  referenced in the statement as `$name`. Values can be strings, numbers, booleans, lists or maps.
- `metrics` (optional): one or more metric definitions, see [Metrics](#metrics).
- `logs` (optional): one or more log definitions, see [Logs](#logs).
- `tracking_column` (optional): applies only to logs. Column whose value from the last returned row is passed as a
  query parameter on the next run, see [Tracking processed results](#tracking-processed-results).
- `tracking_start_value` (optional): applies only to logs. Value of the tracking parameter on the first run. The YAML
  scalar type is preserved: `10000` is passed as an integer, `"10000"` as a string.
- `tracking_parameter` (optional, default `tracking_value`): name of the Cypher parameter that carries the tracking
  value, referenced in the statement as `$tracking_value`.
- `ignore_null_values` (optional, default `false`): when `true`, suppresses the warning logged when a row contains a
  `null` in a column that is not referenced by any metric or log definition.

Queries are executed with read routing (`ExecuteQueryWithReadersRouting`). On a cluster they are sent to follower or
read-replica members, so statements that write to the graph are not supported.

#### Logs

Each `logs` entry produces one log record per returned row:

- `body_column` (required): the column whose value becomes the log record body (as a string; lists, maps and graph
  entities are rendered as JSON).
- `attribute_columns` (optional): columns whose values are set as log record attributes (as strings, keyed by the
  column name).
- `ts_column` (optional): column providing the log record timestamp. When omitted only the observed timestamp is set.

##### Tracking processed results

With a plain query such as `MATCH (e:Event) RETURN e.message AS message` the receiver returns the same rows on every
collection interval. To read each row only once, use a parameterized query together with `tracking_column` and
`tracking_start_value`:

```yaml
queries:
  - cypher: "MATCH (e:Event) WHERE e.id > $tracking_value RETURN e.id AS id, e.message AS message ORDER BY e.id"
    tracking_column: id
    tracking_start_value: 0
    logs:
      - body_column: message
```

On the first run `$tracking_value` is `tracking_start_value`. After every run the value of `tracking_column` in the
last returned row becomes the new `$tracking_value`. Sort the results in ascending order of the tracking column so
that the last row really is the newest one.

Integers, floats, booleans and strings are passed to Cypher with their native type. Temporal values (`datetime`,
`date`, ...) are passed as their ISO 8601 string and must be converted back in the query, for example
`WHERE e.at > datetime($tracking_value)`. Set `tracking_parameter` to use a different parameter name than
`tracking_value`.

Without the `storage` option the tracking value only lives in memory and the receiver restarts from
`tracking_start_value` after a collector restart. Configure a storage extension to persist it:

```yaml
extensions:
  file_storage:
    directory: /var/lib/otelcol/storage

receivers:
  neo4j_query:
    uri: bolt://localhost:7687
    username: neo4j
    password: ${env:NEO4J_PASSWORD}
    storage: file_storage
    queries:
      - cypher: "MATCH (e:Event) WHERE e.at > datetime($tracking_value) RETURN e.at AS at, e.message AS message, e.level AS level ORDER BY e.at"
        tracking_column: at
        tracking_start_value: "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
        logs:
          - body_column: message
            attribute_columns: [level]
            ts_column: at

service:
  extensions: [file_storage]
```

#### Metrics

Each `metrics` entry produces one OTel metric per collection with one data point per returned row
(or per row matching `row_condition`):

- `metric_name` (required): the name assigned to the OTel metric.
- `value_column` (required): the column whose value becomes the data point value.
- `data_type` (optional): `gauge` or `sum`; defaults to `gauge`.
- `value_type` (optional): `int` or `double`; defaults to `int`.
- `monotonic` (optional): whether a cumulative sum only increases; defaults to `false`.
- `aggregation` (optional): only for `data_type: sum`; `cumulative` or `delta`, defaults to `cumulative`.
- `description` (optional): metric description.
- `unit` (optional): metric unit.
- `attribute_columns` (optional): columns whose values are set as data point attributes (as strings, keyed by the
  column name).
- `static_attributes` (optional): fixed attributes added to every data point.
- `start_ts_column` (optional): column providing the start timestamp of cumulative sums. Defaults to the receiver
  start time.
- `ts_column` (optional): column providing the data point timestamp. Defaults to the collection time.
- `row_condition` (optional): only rows where `column` equals `value` (compared as strings) produce this metric.
  Useful for pivot-style results such as `CALL dbms.queryJmx(...)` output or `SHOW TRANSACTIONS`.

#### Value conversion

Cypher values arrive with their native types and are converted as follows:

| Cypher value                                     | `value_type: int`             | `value_type: double` | attribute / `row_condition` string   | `ts_column` / `start_ts_column`      |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------ |
| INTEGER                                          | as is                         | converted            | decimal string                       | nanoseconds since Unix epoch         |
| FLOAT                                            | only when integral, else error| as is                | shortest decimal string (`2`, `2.5`) | nanoseconds when integral            |
| BOOLEAN                                          | `1` / `0`                     | `1` / `0`            | `true` / `false`                     | error                                |
| STRING                                           | parsed                        | parsed               | as is                                | parsed as nanoseconds                |
| DATETIME / ZONED DATETIME                        | error                         | error                | RFC 3339 (`2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`)    | the instant                          |
| LOCAL DATETIME, DATE                             | error                         | error                | ISO 8601 (`2026-01-01T00:00:00`)     | the instant, in the collector's zone |
| DURATION, TIME, LOCAL TIME, POINT                | error                         | error                | driver string form (`P1M2DT3S`)      | error                                |
| LIST, MAP, NODE, RELATIONSHIP, PATH              | error                         | error                | JSON                                 | error                                |
| `null`                                           | error                         | error                | error                                | error                                |

A row that fails conversion for a metric produces no data point for that metric and is reported as part of a
partial scrape error; the remaining rows are still delivered.

### Example

```yaml
receivers:
  neo4j_query:
    uri: neo4j://graph.example.com:7687
    username: monitoring
    password: ${env:NEO4J_PASSWORD}
    database: movies
    collection_interval: 30s
    timeout: 10s
    queries:
      - cypher: "MATCH (m:Movie) WHERE m.released >= $since RETURN m.genre AS genre, count(*) AS count"
        parameters:
          since: 2000
        metrics:
          - metric_name: movie.count
            value_column: count
            attribute_columns: [genre]
            static_attributes:
              graph: movies
      - cypher: "MATCH (m:Movie) RETURN avg(m.rating) AS avg_rating, max(m.rating) AS max_rating"
        metrics:
          - metric_name: movie.rating.avg
            value_column: avg_rating
            value_type: double
          - metric_name: movie.rating.max
            value_column: max_rating
            value_type: double
      - cypher: "CALL dbms.queryJmx('org.neo4j:instance=kernel#0,name=Transactions') YIELD attributes RETURN attributes.NumberOfOpenTransactions.value AS open_tx"
        metrics:
          - metric_name: neo4j.transactions.open
            value_column: open_tx
```

Given three `Movie` nodes released after 2000, two of genre `sci-fi` and one of genre `action`, the first query
returns:

| genre  | count |
| ------ | ----- |
| sci-fi | 2     |
| action | 1     |

and the receiver produces one `movie.count` gauge with two data points per collection:

```
Metric #0
Descriptor:
     -> Name: movie.count
     -> DataType: Gauge
NumberDataPoints #0
Data point attributes:
     -> genre: STRING(sci-fi)
     -> graph: STRING(movies)
Value: 2
NumberDataPoints #1
Data point attributes:
     -> genre: STRING(action)
     -> graph: STRING(movies)
Value: 1
```

#### Row condition example

`SHOW` commands and many procedures return one row per item. Use `row_condition` to pick individual rows:

```yaml
receivers:
  neo4j_query:
    uri: bolt://localhost:7687
    username: neo4j
    password: ${env:NEO4J_PASSWORD}
    queries:
      - cypher: "SHOW DATABASES YIELD name, currentStatus RETURN name, CASE currentStatus WHEN 'online' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS online"
        metrics:
          - metric_name: neo4j.database.online
            value_column: online
            attribute_columns: [name]
          - metric_name: neo4j.database.system.online
            value_column: online
            row_condition:
              column: name
              value: system
```

### Differences from the SQL Query Receiver

- Connection is configured with a single `uri` plus `username`/`password`/`database` instead of `driver` and
  `datasource`.
- `cypher` replaces `sql`, and named `parameters` are supported natively.
- The tracking value is passed as a named Cypher parameter (`$tracking_value` by default, configurable with
  `tracking_parameter`) instead of a positional placeholder, keeps its type (integer, float, string) and is stored as
  JSON in the storage extension.
- Log records accept an optional `ts_column`.
- Values keep their Cypher types, so integers, floats, temporal values and graph entities are converted explicitly
  (see [Value conversion](#value-conversion)) instead of going through a driver-specific string representation.
- Each metric definition yields one metric with one data point per row instead of one single-point metric per row.
- Rows that fail conversion are skipped instead of producing a zero-valued data point or an empty log record.
- `timeout` is applied to every query execution.

## Development

Unit tests run without a database:

```sh
cd receiver/neo4jqueryreceiver
go test ./...
```

The integration test covers metrics and tracked logs; it starts a `neo4j:5` container through testcontainers and requires Docker:

```sh
go test -tags integration -run TestIntegration -v ./...
```
